A STANDING BUILT ACROSS TWO DECADES

For twenty years, Dr. K has stood at the intersection of government, reputation, and African transition. Shaping how nations are perceived, how institutions are built, and how legacies are preserved.

Her work has touched the rebuild of South Africa’s economic identity at the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition. The reputation of the country during its first energy crisis at Eskom. The transition of the broadcasting industry to digital. The protocol of Tata Nelson Mandela’s final send-off. And the founding of pan-African institutions that move capital, culture, and consciousness forward.

She does not consult. She convenes.

Six chapters. One throughline: stewardship of African institutions.

2002 to 2006

Marketing Officer · Relationship Manager · Acting Advertising Manager

Architected the dtic brand positioning strategy adopted by Parliament as a blueprint for all government departments. Her signature is engraved on the dtic campus wall of fame.

2006 to 2007

Headhunted to establish the national environmental endorsement brand for the Department of Environment and Tourism. Led the South African expo at the World Summit on Sustainable Development.

2007 to 2008

Reputation Specialist & Senior Strategist

Developed the Defend and Grow capability strategy. Managed the corporate reputation of Telkom as a JSE-listed entity through industry transition.

2008 to 2014

Reputation Management Specialist

2010 to 2014

National Communication Task Team

Member · Chairperson (2014)

Chaired national consultations with SABC, ICASA, MultiChoice, MASA and CNBC charting South Africa’s digital television transition. Co-shaped the Mzansi Golden Economy strategy and the 90/10 local content policy.

2006 to 2016

Project M & National Service

Founding Member, Progressive Youth in Business · Project M Protocol

Member of the protocol and strategic communications team for Tata Nelson Mandela’s passing and send-off. Editor of Impressions of an Icon. Executive Producer of the SABC documentary series Mother of the Nation.

She is not a consultant building a portfolio. She is a custodian extending a tradition.

THE FULL ACCOUNTING

A diplomat shaped by the African experience.

HRH Ambassador Dr. Khumoetsile Moetse holds the royal title of Princess of Bataba boo Lekoma. She is an institutional leader, diplomat, global humanitarian, entrepreneur, and a proud mother of two.

Her career began at the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition, where her brand positioning strategy was adopted by Parliament as a blueprint for all government departments, and where her signature remains engraved on the dtic campus wall of fame among those who led South Africa’s economic transition post-democracy.

She served as Reputation Management Specialist at Eskom Holdings during South Africa’s first energy crisis, and as Senior Strategist at Telkom Limited where she developed the Defend and Grow capability strategy. As National Chairperson of the Communication Task Team, she led national consultations with SABC, ICASA, CNBC, MultiChoice and MASA, shaping broadcasting policy, local content, and the country’s transition to digital television.

She was a member of Project M, the protocol and strategic communications team for Tata Nelson Mandela’s passing and send-off, and served as editor of Impressions of an Icon. She was Executive Producer of Mother of the Nation, the SABC documentary series on the life of Mama Winnie Madikizela-Mandela.

Today, she leads across multiple boards and ventures: Founder of Africa Media Fund, Executive Director of Silla Global AI, Chairperson of Silla Green Consortium, Founder of Black Pearls Foundation, and Lead Consultant at Etsile Wealth Holdings.

Dr. K is a Goodwill Ambassador to the Kingdom of Eswatini, and the holder of a Doctorate of Philosophy from Trinity International University of Ambassadors and an Honorary Doctorate in Humanitarianism from GIA University USA.
